findings.evidence: In dom-1440.json the seven category h2s ("Interactions" at y=317 to "Design" at y=6313) are 16px, the same size as the body and the bold rule leads under them ("Keyboard works everywhere.", "Clear focus."). findings.evidence: The page has no nav landmark and no list of categories; the first screen goes from the intro paragraph straight into the 119 rule items (the start-line count gives 119 blocks at x=380). The category heads are anchor links, so targets exist, but nothing links to them. The page is 8,815px tall at 1440 and 14,211px at 375.
findings.before: A long single-column reference with no table of contents.
findings.after: Add a short list of the category anchors under the intro, or a sticky list in the empty left margin at 1440 (the column starts at x=360).
findings.why: Reference pages are read by jumping to a category; without a contents list the reader scrolls or uses find-in-page.

findings.title: Weight steps are clear
findings.evidence: dom-1440.json gives every section head at 16px, weight 500, white, 24px line height. The bold lead-in of each rule below it ("Keyboard works everywhere.") is also 16px, at weight 550 in #ededed. The body text is 16px at 400. The type table finds only two size steps on the page: the 32px h1 and 16px for everything else. A section head is therefore lighter than the rule titles it groups, and only the space above it marks it.
findings.after: Section heads one clear step up (for example 20 to 24px at weight 600), so the h1, section and rule levels each have their own size
findings.why: In a long list of rules the reader scans for the section, and a head lighter than its own items does not stop the eye.
findings.fix: Move the two roles to weights far enough apart to see, or separate them by size.

findings.title: Punctuation is typeset and consistent
findings.evidence: The type table counts 30 straight and 32 curly double quotes, 2 straight and 15 curly apostrophes, and 1 three-dot run against 8 true ellipses. Some straight marks sit correctly inside code (content="width=device-width..."), but others are prose: "Rename…", "Loading…" and "Saving…" in the ellipsis rule use straight double quotes, and "selection/hover don't occur" uses a straight apostrophe a few lines below "Don’t leave users guessing" with a curly one.
findings.after: Curly quotes and apostrophes in all prose; straight marks only inside code elements
findings.why: The mix shows on the same screen, on a page whose own copy rules ask for typeset punctuation.
findings.fix: Normalise quotes at the content source; join numbers and units with a non-breaking space.
